## Proposal and provenance

Stable algorithm slug: `coverage-preserving-budget-truncation`. Source: pm-4k6b note recorded 2026-08-13T21:15:51.685Z.

Signal candidate (43) — coverage-preserving budget truncation: when a read cannot return everything, the retained subset is selected to represent the withheld one rather than to be its prefix. Measured 2026-08-13.

Candidates (39) through (42) all answer one question: given a candidate set and a budget, how should items be scored so the best rank first. This candidate answers a different one, which the engine does not currently ask at all: given that the budget will drop rows, which subset should survive.

## The measurement that forces it

The universal read-output budget shipped and now binds. On this workspace, pm list --status open returns 85 of 341 open rows under the default 6,000-token toon ceiling. The selection rule is in compactRowsToBudget: take the largest row collection, splice off half from the tail, re-estimate, repeat. The retained set is therefore a prefix of whatever order the command applied, which for list is the default order and is neither relevance nor recency.

The retained sample is not close to representative. Retained versus dropped, by type:

  type       retained   dropped   retained share
  Issue            41        86             32%
  Epic             12         8             60%
  Task             15        60             20%
  Feature          12        50             19%
  Chore             2        24              8%
  Decision          1         7             13%
  Milestone         2         5             29%
  Story             0        13              0%
  Plan              0         2              0%
  Reminder          0         1              0%

Three whole item types survive at zero. Every Story — the layer this project uses to state what an agent or an organisation needs from the product — is invisible to a caller who asks what is open. So is every Plan.

The family skew is sharper than the type skew. Of the 51 open items whose titles begin Semgrep, Scorecard or DeepSource, exactly 0 are retained. The entire recorded security and code-quality finding population is absent from the default answer to "what is open", with no signal in the response that a coherent population was removed rather than an arbitrary tail.

And the truncation is not even cost-efficient in its own currency. Mean title length is 139 characters in the retained set against 123 in the dropped set, so tail-splicing systematically keeps the expensive rows and discards the cheap ones. A selection that spent the same tokens on the cheapest rows first would return strictly more rows, and a coverage-aware selection would return strictly more distinct facts per token. The current rule is the worst of the three on both counts.

## The candidate, stated generally

When a bounded read must drop rows, choose the retained subset to maximise coverage of the full result rather than to preserve sort position. This is a cardinality-constrained maximum-coverage selection: retain S subject to cost(S) within budget, maximising the marginal information of S with respect to the full result R.

The concrete rule that fits this codebase, cheapest step first:

Partition the full result by fields the row projection already carries — for list, type and status and declared tags; for search, the matched field; for graph, the edge kind. These are free, already computed, and are the fields a caller filters on next.

Allocate the row budget across partitions proportionally to partition size, with a floor of one row per non-empty partition while budget remains. Largest-remainder apportionment, fully deterministic.

Within a partition, retain by the existing order. Sort order still decides which member of a group survives; it stops deciding which groups survive.

Charge each row its own estimated cost rather than assuming a uniform row, so the budget buys rows instead of buying positions.

Report the shape of what was dropped: per-partition retained and total counts. A handful of integers, and it is the difference between an unrepresentative sample and a described one.

## Why this belongs to this epic and not to the output layer

The output layer knows the ceiling and the rows. It does not know, and should not learn, what makes two rows redundant. That judgement is this engine's, it is the same judgement (39) through (42) make about signal weighting, and it needs the same inputs. Selecting a covering subset is scoring with a diversity term: score(item given S) = relevance(item) minus lambda times max_similarity(item, S). The partition rule above is the zero-cost approximation of exactly that, and it is what should ship first.

The general form is what to reach for where row fields are insufficient — for context and next, where the natural similarity is graph distance rather than field equality. There it composes directly with (42): retain the items that dominate disjoint parts of the graph, which maximises the fraction of the workspace explained per returned row.

## Degeneracy, which this epic requires of every candidate

Below the budget the rule never fires and output is byte-identical to today. On a three-item workspace no read is truncated, so a minutes-old scratch project sees nothing, which is what pm-z436 requires. With one partition it reduces exactly to prefix truncation. With every row in its own partition it reduces to round-robin over the rank order, correct for a maximally heterogeneous set. No scale tier, no fitted threshold.

## Cost

One pass over rows already in memory, on a path that today re-serialises the entire result up to 64 times to converge on its estimate. Selecting the retained set analytically from partition sizes and per-row cost replaces that loop rather than adding to it, so the expected direction on latency is down.

## Relationship to the rest of the roadmap

Horizon AR holds that an emitted forward reference is an unexecuted claim. This is the constructive half of the same finding: once truncation discloses what it dropped, the disclosure creates an obligation to drop well, and a prefix is the worst available choice against it.

The population argument is horizon AQ's, applied to results rather than verdicts. AQ asks what population a passing gate speaks for; this asks what population a returned result speaks for, and answers that a bounded read should be a sample with known bias rather than an arbitrary one. That is precisely the property pm-g2zz needs for a million-item workspace to be readable at all, because at that scale every read is truncated, and under the prefix rule every read describes the same corner of the corpus.

Routing. Candidate only, and it belongs on pm-g8t7b9's portfolio register with a named owner before any weight is committed. Its first landing should be the free partition rule inside the existing budget path, gated by the truncation disclosure shipped alongside this measurement so the effect is measurable rather than asserted.

## Delivery boundary

Evaluate this mechanism as a bounded public-SDK experiment before any production adoption. Use the existing scorer and packer contracts; no CLI-only behavior or new command noun. The historical catalog is design input, not evidence that this mechanism was implemented.

## Experiment protocol

Freeze a workspace/history revision and parameter manifest. Compare against the current deterministic SDK baseline using held-out judgments and negative controls. Report nDCG/action success, critical-evidence omission, latency p50/p95, peak memory, tokens per completed task, and rebuild cost separately. Include 3-item/minutes, real-shaped, 100k/1M-item, decades-long, and sparse/dense/imbalanced graph scenarios; smoke subsets may not claim scale acceptance. Bound candidate counts, graph expansions, elapsed time, and output size, with cancellation and completeness receipts. Record exact versus approximate behavior and approximation error; theoretical guarantees require their stated assumptions. Missing or untrusted evidence remains unknown, never inferred proof.

Promotion requires a reproducible quality improvement on the held-out target population, no regression of existing exact invariants or mandatory gates, and a declared compute/token cost justified by that improvement. Reject or defer with the same immutable evidence if those conditions fail. No production default, adaptive learning, or data export is authorized by this planning item.

Define a versioned public-SDK input/output and parameter contract, with exact source receipts and bounded time, memory and token complexity.; Implement an isolated reproducible prototype and compare held-out quality, task success, costs, cold-start behavior and negative controls against the unchanged baseline.; Record an accept, reject, or defer decision with evidence; production implementation requires an accepted decision and its own linked delivery scope.
A falsifiable decision on coverage preserving budget truncation with reusable benchmark evidence and no unreviewed production policy change.
